mainEntity.name: What is the difference between settling a case and going to trial?

acceptedAnswer.text: Settling a case involves reaching a mutual agreement with the at-fault party or their insurance company outside of court. This typically results in a faster resolution and avoids the uncertainties of a jury verdict. Going to trial means presenting your case before a judge or jury, who then decide the outcome. While a trial can potentially lead to a higher award, it is riskier, more expensive, and significantly more time-consuming. Most car accident cases settle before going to trial.
acceptedAnswer.description: Settling a case is an out-of-court agreement, faster and less risky; going to trial involves a judge or jury verdict, which is slower, costlier, and less predictable.
